## Measuring the Rate of Reaction

* If a gas is produced in the reaction, then the mass will decrease over time.
* A gas syringe or an upside-down measuring cylinder can measure the volume of gas produced.
* Titrations can be used to measure the concentration of a product or reactant at different points in the reaction.
* Colorimetry uses a colourimeter to see a product's formation by measuring the liquid's opacity. A calibration curve is generated by the absorption values, from which a concentration-time graph can be calculated.
